answer: Each epoch the verifier issues a crystal challenge forcing the agent to pin 64 GB of RAM and answer nanosecond latency probes across random offsets within 2 ms, proving physical memory rather than rented compute. A knoll response arriving late or served from swapped pages fails at once and the $500 bond is slashed. One honest agent passes on a single 64 GB node costing $120 a month, while ten fakes need 640 GB across ten separate buses for $1,200 a month, and sparrow audit logs expose any shared hardware. Repeat failures freeze the identity permanently.
